unit.why: A short anecdote: the tzaddik's wife tells his disciple that the master has not eaten since Shabbat, and the master explains that his longing for Torah keeps him from feeling hunger.
unit.boundary_note: Part of a numbered series of praises quoted from the son's introduction; it continues the list from the previous division, but this item is a self-contained anecdote.

stories.start_quote: עוד כתב שם בנו בהקדמתו הנ"ל
stories.summary_en: The tzaddik is so absorbed in the sweetness of Torah that he forgets to eat for days; his wife sends his disciple R. Yehuda Zvi of Rozla to him, and the tzaddik replies that out of longing for Torah he feels no hunger at all.

tags.why: The anecdote illustrates the tzaddik's devotion to Torah.

quotes: שמרוב תשוקת התורה אינני מרגיש כלל
tags.why: His absorption in Torah study is the subject.
Rapt cleaving to the light of Torah.

quotes: לא אכל ולא טעם שום דבר מיום ש"ק עד היום יום חמישי
tags.why: He goes without food from Shabbat to Thursday, though not as a deliberate fast.

quotes: נשכח ד׳ וה׳ ימים מלטעום טעם אוכל ומשקה

tags.why: The tzaddik's wife appears, and the account comes from his son.
The wife speaks and sets the exchange in motion.
An exchange between the master and his disciple.
The anecdote shows the virtue of total devotion to Torah.

missing_concepts: love/longing for Torah (תשוקת התורה) overriding bodily needs
